unstructuredCurriculumRecords.programName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering
unstructuredCurriculumRecords.cohortLabel: 144-credit source plans: 2022-2023-onward Fall and Spring sequences plus a separate Fall-2024-and-prior Fall sequence; applicability and revision precedence unresolved
limitations: The 2022-2023-onward PDF publishes separate Fall-entry and Spring-entry sequences. They are stored as distinct source plans with their printed semester order and subtotals.

A second official PDF is labeled “Cohort fall 2024 and prior” and publishes a different Fall-entry sequence, also totaling 144 credits. Its course set and placement differ from the 2022-2023-onward plan. The official sources do not explain the overlap or establish which revision applies to a particular student.

These three plans are source-separated for lookup only. cohortMapping remains unresolved; do not select a plan by year, merge sequences, infer equivalencies, or treat a model plan as a student Degree Works assignment.

Course-choice rows and CENG xxx elective placeholders are preserved as printed. They are not converted into fixed course requirements. Internship rows retain ITBP495 and 12 credits exactly as shown in these 144-credit source plans; the separate current 131-credit plan and current catalog have their own code/credit facts.

The semester sequence describes published model plans, not current offerings, personal completed credits, prerequisites, or registration eligibility. Confirm the assigned plan with Degree Works or CIT advising.

unstructuredCurriculumRecords.programName: Bachelor of Education in Early Childhood Education
unstructuredCurriculumRecords.cohortLabel: Fall-entry 2020-2021 model-plan cohort; the assigned Degree Works plan controls
limitations: The official 2020-2021 plan labels a Fall-entry model and states a 126-credit total, but the table contains #REF! and blank course-title, credit-hour, and some course-code cells. Complete semester rows, per-course credits, and a reconciled requirement-group model are unavailable from this source. Keep requirements empty, report only the published total, and do not infer missing values from later plans; the student's assigned Degree Works plan must confirm personal applicability.

unstructuredCurriculumRecords.cohortLabel: Students whose assigned plan matches the published 2023-2024 model plan onwards
limitations: The 2023-2024 model-plan PDF publishes 132 credits for Fall and Spring entry. Its named-course set and General Education/course-type labels differ from the current degree page, and its tables contain an ISLM101 line with 0 credits. The course-by-course model is kept unavailable until the zero-credit line and historical course mapping are confirmed against the assigned Degree Works plan.
The PDF has separate Fall-entry and Spring-entry sequences. This total-only record does not establish which sequence or course requirements apply to an individual student.

unstructuredCurriculumRecords.programName: Bachelor of Science in Architectural Engineering
unstructuredCurriculumRecords.cohortLabel: Students whose assigned plan matches the published 2022-2023 model plan
limitations: The official 2022-2023 model plan publishes 147 credits and a 15-credit ARCH495 internship. Its tables use slash-separated legacy/current labels (MATH1110/130, MATH1120/135, MATH2210/270, MATH2220/145), which require careful course identity mapping.

The Fall-entry table lists GENG215 Engineering Ethics (2 credits) twice, while the official 2016-2017 course catalog defines GENG215 as a 2-credit course. The sources do not explain whether the duplicate is intentional or a table error; do not count one pass twice or invent a replacement requirement.

The visually checked Spring-entry semester rows reconcile to the declared 147-credit total and are represented in semesterPlans. The Fall-entry schedule remains fail-closed: the PDF's Fall rows sum to 149, printed subtotals to 144, and declared total is 147; GENG215 appears twice without an explanatory source note.

Slash-separated legacy/current code labels are preserved verbatim. Do not count duplicate GENG215 twice, infer a replacement course, or assign either track to an individual without Degree Works/advising.

This record is available only for a student who explicitly identifies Spring entry and the 2022-2023 Architectural Engineering source plan. It does not assign the student's personal curriculum; confirm Degree Works.

The nine Spring-entry semester subtotals and underlying printed rows reconcile to the declared 147 credits. This models source schedule blocks, not course equivalencies, prerequisites, term offerings, or a personalized degree audit.
Slash-separated course labels are retained exactly as published and are not interpreted as equivalencies. Elective choices remain unnamed because the plan does not enumerate eligible options.

The separate Fall-entry table is not modeled at course level: Semester 3 rows sum to 18 against a printed subtotal of 17, Semester 4 rows sum to 19 against a printed subtotal of 16, the printed subtotals sum to 144, and the listed rows sum to 148 against the 147-credit header. GENG215 is listed in both semesters 2 and 3; the source does not explain the repeated course or other subtotal discrepancies.

programs.requirementCoverageNote: Repeated required courses need source review: a source may intentionally count one course in multiple categories, but a duplicate group can otherwise make a course appear twice. Credit buckets are category totals, not proof that all requirements are structured.

phase2InventoryGate.note: This is a source-inventory gate only. A nonempty requirement group does not certify that a curriculum version models every degree requirement or reconciles to its published total; full requirement coverage review remains separate. Explicit cohort ambiguity, source-conflicted total-only plans, and unparseable prerequisite source text remain unavailable for unsupported planning. This is not factual certification or release approval.

caveats: Counts measure local snapshot coverage, not factual approval or query-answer accuracy.
A curriculum without an unresolved flag is not proof that every historical cohort is covered.
A structurally parsed prerequisite is not an independent validation of its source meaning.
Freshness uses the snapshot's source verification date; it does not check the live website.
